items.entity: volume bound V in the constraint Σρ_i = V (effective volume fraction V/(m·ρ̄))
items.description: Eq. (1) imposes Σρ_i = V, and V appears only symbolically elsewhere (initial ρ_i = V/m in Secs. 3.2/4.1, the 0.8·V plotting rule in Sec. 7.2). Sec. 7, Sec. 7.1 and Table 1 never give a value or fraction for CANT-16-2-2-5. K(ρ) is linear, so V would only rescale the design if ρ̄ never became active. Elements do saturate (Sec. 7.2: solid elements clustered along the boundary), so V/(m·ρ̄) changes the layout.

Eqs. (1), (2), (7) and Algorithm 4 use the upper bound ρ̄_i, but no value is ever given (Sec. 7.1 specifies only the lower bound). ρ̄ = 1 is a natural guess (Fig. 3 hides elements with ρ_i ≤ 0.1), but the text does not state it. For a given V it sets the effective volume fraction and which elements saturate.
readings: uniform ρ̄_i ≠ 1 (e.g. 2 or 10) with V kept as an absolute number, so the bound becomes active in fewer elements

items.description: Sec. 7.1 gives method-dependent lower bounds for this one example: ρ̲ = 0 for PBM and ρ̲ = 1e-7 for IP and DOC. Table 1 adds an IP run with ρ̲ = 1e-3, whose objective (66.1988863) is called not comparable. Sec. 7 also says formulation (1) uses positive lower bounds. A single solver must pick one value, and stiffness-based solvers need ρ̲ > 0 to keep K positive definite.
readings: ρ̲ = 1e-7 (as in the IP and DOC runs; objective ≈ 66.19273)

items.entity: Young's modulus E (scale of element stiffness K_i)
items.description: K_i are described only as stiffness matrices of trilinear hexahedra (Secs. 1, 6.2); no Young's modulus is given anywhere. Compliance scales as 1/E, so the Table 1 value 66.19… cannot be reproduced in absolute terms.

No Poisson's ratio is stated anywhere (Secs. 6.2, 7). It changes the element stiffness K_i (the coupling between shear and normal stiffness), so it can change the optimal 3D density distribution, not just the compliance value.

items.entity: physical edge length of the coarse cubes / fine elements
items.description: Sec. 7 defines the domain as m_x×m_y×m_z = 16×2×2 'cubes of equal size', refined to 256×32×32 elements. This fixes the 8:1:1 proportions but no physical length is given. For a fixed force on 3D trilinear hexahedra, K_e ∝ E·h, so compliance ∝ 1/h.

items.entity: z-load on the right-hand (x = L) face
items.description: Sec. 7 says only that 'a load in direction z is applied in the middle of the right-hand face (Figure 2(a))'. No force value is given, and if the load is distributed it is not said whether the value is the total force or an intensity. Compliance scales as F².

items.entity: z-load 'in the middle of the right-hand face'
items.description: Sec. 7 places the load 'in the middle' of the x = L face (centre, y = W/2, z = H/2) and refers to Fig. 2(a) for the specification, which is not available. A single nodal force at the face-centre node is natural (a centre node exists at every level, since the coarse face is 2×2). A line or patch load through the centre is not ruled out. By contrast, the bridge load is explicitly a rectangle.
readings: point force at the single face-centre node (y = W/2, z = H/2)
line load along the full width (y) at mid-height z = H/2
line load along the full height (z) at mid-width y = W/2
uniform traction on a small square patch centred on the face (e.g. 2×2 or 4×4 fine elements)

items.description: Sec. 7 gives only 'direction z'; whether the load points in +z or −z is presumably shown by the arrow in Fig. 2(a). In linear elasticity, reversing f only reverses u, so neither the compliance nor the optimal ρ changes; listed only for completeness.
